sentences.text: Odoribacter splanchnicus is an anaerobe that normally inhabits the human intestine and rarely causes infections in humans.
A review describes it as widely present in the mammalian gut and able to synthesise various metabolites, especially short-chain fatty acids.
That review reports that changes in its abundance have been found to correlate positively or negatively with health issues such as obesity, metabolic syndrome, diabetes and intestinal inflammation.
A laboratory records search detected five cases of Odoribacter splanchnicus bacteraemia between 2014 and 2024, and notes that all cases reported to date were associated with intestinal infection.
A study of human cohorts and mouse models reported that depletion of Odoribacter splanchnicus impairs intestinal P-glycoprotein function.
